newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell T$450 bln in state stock over 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell T$450 bln in state stock over 3 yrs.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Wednedsay it planned to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years to help balance the government budget and privatise industry.

"We plan to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years to help balance the government budget and privatise state companies," said Cheng Chih-chen, deputy head of the ministry's national treasury department.
Under the tentative plan, the ministry plans to release T$150 billion worth of state shares each year starting from fiscal 1998/99 (July/June), Cheng told Reuters.
"This is still an initial proposal and is subject to change in order not to dampen the stock market due to oversupply of stock," she said.
In the current fiscal year starting July 1, 1997, the government aready has budgeted to sell off T$97 billion worth of state shares, Cheng said.
In fiscal 1997/98, Taiwan was expected to have a government budget deficit of T$96.6 billion, she said.
The government has set a goal of balancing the budget in fiscal 2000/01.
"To reach a balanced budget, the finance ministry will issue government bonds and privatise state companies," Cheng said.
